data: Jaalis: Cutting through from the Past to the Present

The cut work windows, or “jaalis”, as an aesthetic as well as a practical architectural feature, has been used in multiple cultures through history, typically in hot and arid places. This was most famously used, and most well-crafted (in stone), during the Mughal era. Jaalis have been made in wood, stone, ceramics, and even, (rarely), in metal. As this is a ceramics course, we will touch upon all of them and their histories, but concentrate mostly on the designing and making of terracotta clay jaalis.

In this course you will study the history of jaalis and then go through the process of sketching patterns, drawing inspiration from what we see around the campus, to develop and execute your own modular jaali design. You will learn to convert your designs from 2D to 3D and make a sample jaali window section, and fire it. You will learn the processes that the material requires and learn about utility specific design and execution, giving you an appreciation for craft and craftsmanship.
